The phase on the night someone was born is a permanent party fact. This page answers it for any year the cycle can be counted back through.
What lit the battlefield, the crossing, the escape? Phase-by-date reconstructs the Moon's contribution to any dated event — novelists and historians both keep it bookmarked.
'There was a full moon that night' appears in a thousand memoirs. Most are wrong by a week; this is the thirty-second check.

Ask for 12 August 2026 and the answer is new moon — necessarily, because a total solar eclipse crosses Iceland and Spain that day and solar eclipses happen only at new. The model's big dates check out against the sky's biggest events.
21 June 2026 computes to a waxing crescent-to-quarter Moon, age about 6.2 days and roughly 38% lit — a modest evening Moon riding the year's longest day.

popular_table.note: Names and bands follow the mean cycle in the northern-hemisphere view; southern observers see the lit side mirrored. Band edges are conventions — a Moon at 12.95 days is 'full' for every practical purpose.

faq: How far back and forward does it work?

The mean cycle counts indefinitely in both directions, but its error grows slowly with distance from the present era — hours of drift per century-scale jumps, days across millennia. For ancient dates, treat the name as approximate.
My birthday shows a different phase on two sites.

Sites differ in model precision and in which instant of the date they evaluate (midnight UTC versus local evening). A phase near a band edge flips between honest models. The Moon Age Calculator shows the underlying number so you can see how close the call is.
Does the time of day matter?
The Moon ages about half a day across a single date's span of timezones. Borderline dates genuinely have two answers on one planet — pick the evening of the place you mean.

Waxing is growing (the lit part increases toward full), waning is shrinking after full. The old words survive because they are exact: the Moon really does wax and wane like the candle metaphor they came from.
Was there really a full moon on the famous date?

Sometimes. Apollo 11's landing night (20 July 1969) had a waxing crescent a day or so past new in the evening sky over the Pacific — history's most famous Moon was mostly absent from its own landing. Check any claim here in seconds.
Calendar labels, not phases: a blue moon is a second full in a month; a supermoon is a full moon near perigee. Both ride on the phase this page names — the names here stay astronomical.
Can I get the exact full-moon instant?
This page names the phase for a date; the Next Full Moon Calculator targets the event and its timing. Use the pair: date first, precision second.
